newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Juncker, Prodi welcome France's moves to join EMU.
newsitem.headline: Juncker, Prodi welcome France's moves to join EMU.

text.p: Luxembourg's Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker and his Italian counterpart Romano Prodi on Monday welcomed France's renewed commitment to join the monetary union on time after Paris announced new moves to curb the budget deficit.
Speaking at a news conference, Juncker said Italy was on the "right track" to be in the first group of countries launching EMU in January 1999.
"The French decision clearly shows France is committed to EMU and committed to the start date and to making all the efforts needed," Juncker said.
Juncker, who is due to visit France on Tuesday, said he would be able to make a fuller comment following his trip.
"This will be the moment to listen carefully," he said.
Prodi, also present, said that the figures in the French audit were not unexpected.
I appreciate the (French) declaration that France will be in....There are no obstacles, we must go on with the planned agenda."
